description: Spellings the corpus evidence admitted but a recorded review rejected. respelling: a common word written with the wrong diacritics in OCR text (στρατηγού for στρατηγοῦ), among the entries the gate reports as respellings of frequent words. structural: a reviewed-baseline entry that fails the orthography rules and is not a word a writer types (editorial underdots, synizesis ties, spurious extra accents).
method: Two independent reviewers labelled every candidate from its attestation by source and up to three corpus sentences; a form is listed only where both rejected it. αὗθις and ἄπαντα, which both rejected, are kept: GLAUx attests them in held-out text, and a breathing variant may be an edition's own spelling.
